title: Change Annals Usage reporting
summary: Modify how Annals Usage calculates, reports, diagnoses, or authenticates access to Annals-attributed model usage.
use_when: The Annals Usage package, projection semantics, rate-card comparison, configuration, diagnostics, or delegated login surface is changing.
do_not_use_when: The task is to run a current report, budget read, doctor, or login.
The required change belongs to Nucleus output or account authority or to Annals domain state.
A retained reporting database is being proposed without a new explicit product boundary.
outcome: A tested versioned projection change that continues to derive live results from Annals and Nucleus authorities and states every accounting limit explicitly.
effects: Modifies the separately versioned `annals-usage` package, tests, configuration, or telemetry documentation.
May require coordinated Annals attribution or Nucleus output-contract changes when an upstream atomic record changes.
Publication and joint Annals deployment remain separately authorized actions.
authority: Annals Usage owns projection interpretation only.
Annals owns delivery and model-run attribution; Nucleus owns jobs, attempts, exact output atoms, account access, and credentials.
success: Coverage, overlapping token categories, unattributed runs, rate-card limits, and account-global allowance scope remain explicit and tested.
No telemetry database, account snapshot, credential copy, UI scrape, or offline estimate is introduced.
failure_and_recovery: Fail when an underlying authority is unreadable instead of returning a stale cached answer.
Version projection interpretation when derived semantics change and retain atomic authorities needed for historical recalculation.
Coordinate upstream changes through the owning Annals or Nucleus contract rather than duplicating their state.
privacy: Tests and live reports can expose private delivery attribution, model output metadata, account plan, and activity.
Annals Usage must never read or retain Nucleus credential files.
Do not add Semantics repository output to an Annals liaison prompt.
steps: Read `semantics.repository.explore`, query `semantics repository show annals`, read the telemetry contract, and identify whether Annals Usage actually owns the requested meaning.
Run `nucleus manual` before changing shared output, account, authentication, compatibility, or deployment behavior.
Implement the smallest projection change and update telemetry documentation and exact coverage tests.
Run `./annals/ci.sh`; perform separately authorized live report, budget, doctor, and requester canaries when affected.
checkpoints: Atomic source authorities remain Annals and Nucleus records rather than a new reporting store.
Every usage total is coverage-qualified and overlapping categories are not double-counted.
Allowance output remains account-global and is not misrepresented as a delivery denominator.
Release or deployment has not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Update projection decoding according to the exact supported Nucleus harness records while preserving explicit gaps for unknown forms.
Update rate-card comparisons only from the current authoritative pricing source and keep them distinct from invoices.
stop_when: The desired fact cannot be derived from supported Annals and Nucleus authorities.
The change would require Annals Usage to own credentials or runtime state.
An upstream contract change has not been accepted by its owning product.
does_not_authorize: Running the Annals release publication command.
Changing upstream Annals or Nucleus meaning without their owning changes.

consumers.statement: A contributor or interactive development agent may use this operation for an authorized Annals Usage projection, rate-card, configuration, diagnostics, account-access, or delegated-login change.
This operation does not run reports or account commands, create a reporting database, change Annals or Nucleus authority from the companion side, publish a release, or deploy.

preconditions.statement: The contributor has read the installed Semantics exploration contract, complete current annals repository, telemetry contract, and current owning Annals Usage boundary.
Changes to shared output, account, authentication, compatibility, deployment, or requester integration require the installed Nucleus manual and coordinated owner contract before implementation.

inputs.statement: Input is one scoped Annals Usage change request plus current canonical terminology, telemetry documentation, source, tests, and any affected upstream owner contract.
A UI scrape, credential copy, retained aggregate, unqualified estimate, or requester-side redefinition of Annals or Nucleus state is not a valid implementation input.

outputs.statement: The result is the smallest coherent separately versioned projection, test, configuration, and telemetry-documentation change with explicit accounting limits and a green ./annals/ci.sh gate.
Development completion does not itself publish, deploy, mutate live account state, or prove a live report and login canary.

data_semantics.statement: Annals Usage owns disposable live interpretation only; Annals retains source-delivery and model-run attribution, and Nucleus retains jobs, attempts, output, account, and credential authority.
Exact, cumulative, gap, no-model, pending, and reused coverage remain distinct, and overlapping token categories are not additive.
Rate-card equivalent is a comparison rather than an invoice, and allowance remains account-global rather than a per-delivery denominator.

identity_and_units.statement: Annals Usage package and provider versions, projectionVersion, entry contract version, upstream record identities, Nucleus protocol, and Annals schema are distinct evolution axes.
Token categories retain their documented units and subset relationships; external rate-card units remain separate from invoices and account allowance.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Every affected coverage case, attribution gap, rate-card limit, account scope, and upstream decoding boundary is updated explicitly in tests and telemetry documentation.
Completion requires the full Annals product gate and separately authorized live report, budget, doctor, login, or requester canaries when the changed boundary affects them.
No development duration, external rate-card freshness, live-canary availability, or guarantee about unrelated projections is promised.

access.statement: The operation uses the current local workspace, filesystem, and shell through an interactive agent session under Annals repository instructions.
Development authority does not grant credential access, release publication, installed deployment, external disclosure, direct upstream database mutation, or direct Semantics-state editing.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Identify the owning product meaning, update the smallest projection and exact coverage tests, version changed interpretation, update telemetry documentation, then run the full Annals gate.
Atomic Annals and Nucleus records remain the recalculation authorities, and an unreadable upstream fails a live projection rather than causing a stale retained fallback.
Publication and joint Annals deployment remain separately authorized lifecycles after development completion.

operational_limits.statement: No telemetry store, aggregate, snapshot, credential copy, UI scrape, offline estimate, or unqualified gap is permitted, and every code change must leave ./annals/ci.sh green.
No maximum change size, completion time, account availability, or external rate-card service level is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Derived interpretation changes advance projectionVersion and preserve the atomic records required for historical recalculation; upstream changes are coordinated through the owning Annals or Nucleus contract.
Package release, provider release, entry contract version, projectionVersion, Annals schema, and Nucleus protocol are evaluated independently.
No release cadence, rate-card stability, cross-release compatibility window, or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Annals Usage development relies on the registered Semantics repository for current Annals terminology while retaining telemetry documentation and project sources as behavior authority.
A documentation dependency or conditional need to consult an upstream owner must not be interpreted as authority to mutate that upstream product.
